Subject: Re: Brightline MSA — review notes (legal redline)

Thanks for the ping — quick legal notes after a pass on Brightline's proposal and Mina's draft counter. High-level: term and capacity asks are commercially reasonable, but a few legal items need redline language or clarification.

1) Indemnity (Section 10) — Brightline's ask removes Redwood's IP carve-outs for model outputs. Counter: propose mutual indemnity limited to direct IP claims where Redwood had control over the model stack and did not follow customer instructions. Suggested language: "Redwood will indemnify to the extent a third-party IP claim arises from our proprietary model code; customer indemnifies for use of customer-supplied prompts or data that cause infringement."

2) Data retention (Section 8) — 7 years for audit logs is longer than standard. Recommend: 3 years default, 7 years available via a compliance addendum (chargeable). If they want 7 years as part of seat/commitment, Sales to confirm pricing uplift. Also need to scope "audit logs" vs "customer content" — we should not retain full PII beyond our default retention.

3) SLA and capacity — baseline uplift is fine but liability cap should not increase. If Brightline requires higher credits (e.g., doubled credits for the uplift), escalate to execs. We should attach a capacity schedule and call out that burst is best-effort with no SLA for peak bursts beyond baseline.

4) Auto-renew — 24 + 12 auto-renewal OK, but add a 60-day cancellation notice and a price-change pass-through allowance (capped to CPI + 4%).

5) Export controls / compliance — add a short clause that allows Redwood to comply with legal obligations if a specific model or region is restricted.

I made inline comments in Brightline_MSA_redline_2027-10-06.docx and summarized the changes in redline_summary_2027-10-06.pdf. Questions for Sales: is Brightline willing to accept a paid 7-year audit log option? If so, we can include that as Exhibit B (pricing table).

Ben Carter
